clues: This city stands on a wide river in the middle part of its state. Its river port and rail lines helped it grow rich and fast.
Winters here bring snow most years, but it seldom piles up deep. Summers turn hot and damp, in the style of the upper South.
In 1843, this river town was picked as the lasting capital of its state. Three other towns had held the job before, but this one kept it.
The Grand Ole Opry, a live country music radio show, comes from this city. It is the longest running radio broadcast in the land.
Tennessee's top court keeps a courthouse for its middle region in this city. That seat shows the city's key role in state government.
